title: Preface

nodes.title: Preface (intro)
nodes.summary: Unsealed 2018 D.D.C. order (No. 11-mc-44) transmitting the June 5, 1972 Grand Jury's report and recommendation to the House Judiciary Committee. The grand jury returned an indictment, deferred impeachment matters to the House regarding President Nixon, and asked that evidence be used with regard for fair trials. Attached: evidence index covering E. Howard Hunt, the $75,000 payment, the President's 'investigation,' events through March 1973, and public statements.

nodes.title: i. MATERIAL BEARING ON A $75,000 PAYMENT TO E. HOWARD HUNT AND RELATED EVENTS.
nodes.summary: Covers E. Howard Hunt's March 16, 1973 meeting with Paul O'Brien, where Hunt demanded about $120,000 and said he had done 'seamy things' for the White House and John Ehrlichman, warning he would 'review his options' if unpaid. Also notes O'Brien relaying Hunt's message to John Dean on March 19, 1973. Includes grand jury testimony citations from Hunt and O'Brien (1973-1974).

summary: Unsealed 2018 D.D.C. order (No. 11-mc-44) transmits the June 5, 1972 Grand Jury report and recommendation to the House Judiciary Committee. The grand jury indicted, deferred impeachment of President Nixon to the House, and urged fair-trial considerations. Attached evidence index covers E. Howard Hunt, the $75,000 payment, the President's 'investigation,' events through March 1973, and public statements. Hunt's March 16, 1973 meeting with Paul O'Brien demanded about $120,000, and O'Brien relayed it to John Dean on March 19, 1973, with grand jury testimony cited.

title: 2.1 Grand Jury Testimony of John Dean, February
summary: The text is a document excerpt with citations: John Dean's February 1974 grand jury testimony (pp. 13-14), and a U.S. Secret Service record of a March 19, 1973, 5:20 p.m. White House appointment for Paul O'Brien (FOIA #58707). It also states that on or about March 19, 1973, Dean spoke with John Ehrlichman, relaying Hunt's message, and Ehrlichman asked Dean to pass it to John Mitchell.

title: 3.4 Grand Jury Testimony 13, 1973, pp. 2-6.
summary: The text is a citation fragment from a FOIA-released document (FOIA # 58707, Docld 70105890, page 7). It lists grand jury testimony references: a 1973 testimony (pp. 2-6), a 1974 testimony (pp. 5-10), and Item 2.1 (p. 14), including testimony of John Ehrlichman (September 13, 1973) and Egil Krogh (January 29, 1974).

title: 4. On or about March 20, John Dean had a conversation with John Mitchell concerning Hunt's message.
summary: Describes a March 21, 1973 meeting between the President and John Dean (Haldeman present part of the time) covering involvement of named officials in obstruction of justice and perjury; E. Howard Hunt's $120,000 demand and threat to disclose 'seamy things'; money needed to keep Watergate defendants silent and how to deliver it; expectations of help on jail time; likelihood of public disclosure; whether to pay Hunt to 'buy time'; and possible courses of action. Also cites Dean's grand jury testimony and the related tape recording and transcript.

title: 5. (cont.)

nodes.summary: Source text is a Watergate-era FOIA document (FOIA #58707, Docld 70105890, pages 10-11) listing evidence references: a Dictabelt recording and transcript of March 21, 1973 with the President's recollections; tape recordings and transcripts of June 4, 1973 and April 16, 1973 meetings; a telephone conversation of about 12:30 p.m. March 21, 1973 between H. nodes.title: 7.1 Grand Jury Testimony of Fred LaRue, February 13, 1974, pp. 7-10A.
nodes.summary: The text is an excerpt of Watergate-era grand jury testimony and FOIA records. It cites Fred LaRue's February 13, 1974 grand jury testimony (pp. 7-10A) and John Dean's February 1974 testimony (p. 17). It states that on March 21, 1973, at about 3:45 p.m., H. R. Haldeman met with John Ehrlichman and John Dean to discuss possible courses of action on matters raised by the President, Haldeman, and Dean that morning. Includes FOIA #58707 and document ID markers.

nodes.title: 8.2 Meeting 8.3 Meeting
nodes.summary: Describes Nixon-era Watergate materials: transcripts and logs of March 21, 1973 meetings among the President, Dean, Haldeman, and Ehrlichman, including rejected courses of action (new grand jury or independent panel testimony) and discussion of Hunt's demands. Also covers Fred LaRue's late-evening delivery of $75,000 in cash for E. Howard Hunt to Bittman's mailbox, with listed grand jury testimony and exhibits from LaRue, Millican, Unger, Bittman, and Hunt.

nodes.summary: Covers the March 21, 1973 late-evening placement of $75,000 in cash for E. Howard Hunt in the mailbox of Hunt's attorney Bittman, arranged by Fred LaRue. Lists grand jury materials: LaRue testimony (Feb 13, 1974, pp. 2-6); Manyon Millican testimony (Feb 13, 1974); Sherman Unger testimony (Feb 19, 1974); and Grand Jury Exhibits SU-1 through SU-7 (Feb 19, 1974).

nodes.title: 10.5 Grand Jury Testimony of William O. Bittman, August 3, 1973, pp. 189-191, 194-196.
nodes.summary: Excerpts from Nixon-era Watergate materials (FOIA #58707): grand jury testimony citations from Bittman, Hunt, Dean, Haldeman, Ehrlichman, and Krogh. Covers a March 21, 1973 meeting with Dean where Mitchell said Hunt was a problem, and the March 22, 1973 afternoon meeting with the President, Mitchell, Haldeman, Ehrlichman, and Dean about Dean preparing a written report denying high White House involvement in the break-in. Also notes Ehrlichman telling Krogh to "hang tough" and that Hunt was "more stable" and would not "disclose all."

summary: Section 5 (cont.) covers Watergate-era FOIA #58707 evidence on March 21, 1973 events: a Dictabelt recording and President's recollections; a Haldeman-Mitchell call and Haldeman's phone log; grand jury testimony from Haldeman, Dean, and LaRue; Haldeman, Ehrlichman, and Dean's afternoon meeting; Mitchell authorizing LaRue to pay about $75,000 to E. Howard Hunt, delivered that night to attorney Bittman's mailbox (with Millican and Unger testimony); Bittman's testimony; and the March 22 meeting on Dean's written report denying White House involvement.

title: II. MATERIAL BEARING ON THE PRESIDENT'S

nodes.title: II. MATERIAL BEARING ON THE PRESIDENT'S (intro)
nodes.summary: Covers Nixon-era Watergate material (FOIA #58707, pages 20-23). On March 26, 1973, Ronald Ziegler publicly stated the President had 'absolute and total' confidence in counsel John Dean. On March 27-28, 1973, Ehrlichman spoke with Richard Kleindienst, saying the President's best information was that no White House staff had prior knowledge of the break-in, but questions about John Mitchell were raised. On March 30, 1973, the President directed Ehrlichman to examine Dean's work, advise on privilege, and find where the truth lies. Sources cited include grand jury and Senate testimony, wire clips, and dictabelt recordings.

nodes.title: in a public
nodes.summary: Excerpts from Watergate-related documents (FOIA #58707, Docld 70105890, pages 24-26): Ronald Ziegler's 1974 grand jury testimony denying White House involvement; a March 1973 press briefing transcript; an April 15, 1973 meeting where Kleindienst and Henry Petersen urged the President to fire Haldeman and Ehrlichman over implication in Watergate, based on prosecutor information from John Dean and Jeb Magruder; and the President's April 15, 1973 meeting with Dean, in which the President said he had been 'joking' about a million dollars and had been foolish to discuss clemency for E. Howard Hunt with Charles Colson.

nodes.title: 21. At or about 11:45 p.m. on April 15, 1973, the President had a telephone conversation with Henry Petersen.
nodes.summary: Summarizes Watergate-era grand jury testimony and tape-recording references covering the President's April 1973 activities: telephone call with Henry Petersen (April 15), morning and afternoon meetings with John Dean (April 16) on public statements, Dean's testimony, and payments to Hunt, numerous Petersen conversations (April 15-28), Haldeman and Ehrlichman meetings (April 15-30), Petersen's instruction not to investigate the Ellsberg psychiatrist break-in (April 18), and Haldeman's review of the March 21 tape (April 25-26).

summary: Nixon-era Watergate material (FOIA #58707): Ziegler's March 26, 1973 statement of 'absolute and total' confidence in counsel John Dean; Ehrlichman's March 27-28 call with Kleindienst on staff knowledge and Mitchell; the President's March 30 directive to Ehrlichman on Dean's work and privilege. Also grand jury and Senate testimony excerpts, April 15, 1973 meetings urging firing of Haldeman and Ehrlichman, the 'joking' about a million dollars and Hunt clemency remarks, and April 1973 Petersen, Dean, Haldeman, and Ehrlichman contacts. Includes Haldeman's tape notes and June 4, 1973 Haig tape conversation.

nodes.title: 29. On April 4, 1972, the President met with Messrs. H. R. Haldeman and John Mitchell, at which time certain campaign decisions made by Mitchell at Key Biscayne, Florida, on
nodes.summary: On April 4, 1972, the President met with H. R. Haldeman and John Mitchell to review campaign decisions Mitchell made at Key Biscayne on or about March 30, 1972, including approving a budget of about $250,000 for a CRP intelligence program headed by G. Gordon Liddy. Cited sources include grand jury testimony from Jeb S. Magruder, Fred LaRue, Robert Reisner, and John Dean, a log of Haldeman's conversations with the President, and Haldeman's Senate Select Committee testimony (Grand Jury Exhibit RS).

nodes.title: Item 42.1, tape recording and transcript of a morning meeting on March 13, 1973, Tr. 40-41.
nodes.summary: Excerpts from a Watergate-era FOIA-released document (FOIA #58707) listing numbered items and events: Haldeman's knowledge of January-February 1972 meetings in Mitchell's office on unlawful electronic surveillance; the June 20, 1972 Haldeman-Nixon meeting with ~18 minutes of subpoenaed tape obliterated; a June 20 Nixon-Mitchell call whose tape was withheld; the June 28, 1972 approval of Kalmbach distributing covert funds; a June 30 Nixon-Haldeman-Mitchell meeting tape; Gray's July 6 warning that Watergate 'might lead higher'; Ehrlichman's July 1972 clemency talk; and the September 15, 1972 Nixon-Haldeman-Dean meeting. Cites grand jury testimony, tapes, diaries, and dictabelt items.

nodes.title: September 15, 1972, and transcript thereof.
nodes.summary: Excerpts from Watergate-era FOIA-released records (FOIA #58707) covering: a September 15, 1972 transcript and H. R. Haldeman's notes of a meeting and tape listening (Item 37); early Dec 1972 and Jan 1973 Haldeman approval of $350,000 from a secret White House cash fund for payments to Watergate defendants, with grand jury testimony from Dean and Haldeman (Item 38); a late February 1973 Dean-Ehrlichman conversation on whether Executive Privilege would hold for Dean's testimony (Item 39); a February 28, 1973 meeting of the President, Dean, and Mitchell on clemency for Watergate defendants and CRP's role, with tape and transcript (Item 40); a March 13, 1973 meeting on Strachan, Stans, Kalmbach, Sloan, Magruder, Haldeman, Liddy's program, and full disclosure, with tape and transcript (Item 42); and a March 17, 1973 meeting that is cut off (Item 43).

summary: Watergate-era FOIA #58707 excerpts covering events through March 17, 1973: an April 4, 1972 Nixon meeting with Haldeman and Mitchell reviewing Mitchell's Key Biscayne decisions, including a ~$250,000 CRP intelligence budget for G. Gordon Liddy; a series of June-September 1972 items on surveillance knowledge, obliterated and withheld tapes, covert fund approvals, Gray's warning, clemency talk, and a Sept 15, 1972 meeting; Dec 1972-Jan 1973 approval of $350,000 from a White House cash fund for defendants; and Feb-March 1973 meetings on Executive Privilege, clemency, and full disclosure, ending with a cut-off March 17, 1973 meeting. Sources include grand jury testimony, tapes, transcripts, and diaries.

title: On May 22, 1973, the President said in a public statement that "[nJeither did I know until the time of my own
summary: Quotes two public statements by the President: on May 22, 1973, he said he did not know of efforts to fund the Watergate defendants until his own investigation starting March 21, 1973; on August 15, 1973, he said he was told March 21, 1973 that money was raised for defendants' attorney fees and family support, not to procure silence. Cites accompanying statement footnotes.

title: 44.3 Statement by the Preident, August 15, 1973, p. 2.
summary: Excerpts from a Watergate-era document of presidential statements and evidence references. Covers the President's public denials of knowledge of clemency offers and cover-up (May, August, November 1973), his claims of learning of Watergate's broader planning only on March 21, 1973, and his August 1972 and March 1973 statements that no White House staff were involved. Also cites John Dean's grand jury testimony, MacGregor's investigation assurances, and supporting tape recordings and transcripts.

title: On April 30, 1973, the President said in a public statement that, as a result of new information received on March 21, 1973, "I again ordered that all persons in the Government or at the Re~election Committee should cooperate fully with
summary: Excerpts from Nixon-era Watergate records: the President's April 30, 1973 statement that he ordered full cooperation with the FBI, prosecutors and Grand Jury after new information on March 21, 1973; his August 22, 1973 press conference remark about pressing to get the truth out at a March 22 meeting; and his August 15, 1973 statement on Ehrlichman's independent inquiry after Dean's report was incomplete, with cited tapes, transcripts and grand jury testimony.

title: 51. On April 17, 1973, the President said in a public statement that he had met on April 15, 1973, with Richard Kleindienst and Henry Petersen "to review the facts which had come to me in my investigation
summary: Covers three Nixon-era Watergate statements tied to the record: an April 17, 1973 statement that the President met Kleindienst and Petersen on April 15 to review investigation facts; an August 22, 1973 press conference remark that he assumed Dean was telling Petersen everything, and implied the same of Ehrlichman after March 30, 1973; and an August 15, 1973 statement calling March 21 allegations general and unsupported, later supplemented by Ehrlichman's April 14 report, Kleindienst and Petersen's April 15 information, and his own inquiries.
